summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, multiple prior surgeries, and PTSD was admitted for abdominal pain and distention. Imaging revealed colonic ileus without obstruction, and she was managed conservatively with NG tube decompression, NPO status, and pain control. She also had community-acquired pneumonia with right upper lobe consolidation, treated with a 5-day course of levofloxacin. Her bowel function gradually improved, allowing NG tube removal and diet advancement. A PICC line was placed for reliable access due to her history of line infections and venous compromise. She stabilized, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with prescriptions for pain, nausea, anxiety, and anticoagulation, with plans for outpatient follow-up on her lung findings and Crohn’s management.
